clue.text: Hooligan has to vamoose

definitions.meaning: to rush off hurriedly, to dash away

explanation.surface: A thug is told to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a reckless youth is a common British label, and to depart in a hurry is a phrasal verb meaning flee.

clue.text: Mocks relation resident in back-street

indicators.note: something resident lives inside, so one piece is placed within the other
back tells us the abbreviation for street is written backwards

parts.note: an aunt is a family relation

explanation.surface: A family member living down a back alley is jeered at.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean jeers or insults aimed at someone.

clue.text: Insist on getting a lock-up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Demanding a garage or a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock-up' looks like a garage or cell; split it: 'lock' is TRESS and 'up' reverses A + TRESS in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain or state firmly is to insist.

clue.text: Somewhat embarrassed by displaying tapestry

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Someone a little embarrassed at being shown a wall hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich wall hanging of woven fabric, named after the French town famous for it.

clue.text: A bachelor only taking shellfish

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a degree
alone means only, as in 'he alone'

explanation.surface: A single man ordering only seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: An edible sea mollusc with an ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.

clue.text: Cloth sample gets a second look

parts.note: to watch is to look at

explanation.surface: A fabric sample is given another glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece of fabric used to show what the material is like.

clue.text: Healthy living is essential for it

definitions.text: Healthy living is essential for it

parts.words: Healthy living is essential for it
parts.note: read cryptically, being well and being alive together describe a state of good health and happiness

explanation.surface: Advice that clean living matters for good health.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue splits as 'Healthy' = WELL and 'living' = BEING, the whole describing the state those words name.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of being comfortable, healthy and happy, which a healthy life leads to.

clue.text: Brawny, not brainy, this group?

parts.note: thick is slang for stupid
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A question whether a muscular crowd might be lacking in intellect.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocky and heavily built, as a strong person is.

clue.text: Tower gets big increase

definitions.meaning: a tall building of many storeys
a large upward climb, as in a steep rise

explanation.surface: A skyscraper sees prices go up sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: A multi-storey block is called this, and a steep climb is a lofty upward jump.

clue.text: Superior master mistakenly going against the current

parts.note: up means above or superior in position

indicators.note: done mistakenly means the letters of the word master are muddled

explanation.surface: A senior teacher wrongly swimming against the flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving towards a river's source is moving against the flow.

clue.text: Fellow reclining in a plane

parts.note: lying means reclining

explanation.surface: A man lying back in his aircraft seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aloft in an aircraft is travelling by air.

clue.text: Longing for enchanting lady to lose her head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a witch is a woman who casts spells, or enchants

explanation.surface: Desire for a charming woman who is then beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or desire.

clue.text: Debate the possibility of a garden party

definitions.meaning: to discuss thoroughly until a matter is settled

definitions.text: the possibility of a garden party
definitions.meaning: a lively party, or bash, held out of doors

explanation.surface: Discussing whether to hold a party in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue a matter through is one sense; a 'thrash' is slang for a party, and one held outside fits the second.

clue.text: Rider who led Eisenhower into Britain

indicators.note: into means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US general and president Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: A horseman who led the American general into Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcyclist is one who rides a bike.

clue.text: Peak of perfection for bill and yours truly

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
yours truly is the speaker, me

explanation.surface: Top marks for the invoice and for me.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point of achievement, the summit.

clue.text: Ring off and have a lucky escape

definitions.meaning: to end a phone conversation, shutting down a call
a narrow escape, a near miss

explanation.surface: Hanging up the phone and escaping by luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is cryptic: to ring off is to close a call.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is the usual sense; hanging up the phone is the playful second.

clue.text: She succeeds in getting her first series broadcast

indicators.note: her first means only the first letter of the word her
broadcast means scattered, so the letters of series are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman wins with her first TV series being aired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She succeeds' reads like a woman winning, but means one who inherits; 'broadcast' rearranges the letters of 'series', which follow the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter who inherits is one who succeeds to a fortune.

clue.text: Lime for singer and old conductor

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer
Sir Henry Wood was the conductor who founded the Proms

explanation.surface: Fruit for a vocalist and an elderly orchestra leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Lime here is the tree, not the fruit; Sir Henry Wood founded London's Proms concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: The American linden or lime tree has soft pale timber of that name.

clue.text: It's pearl emending the column

indicators.note: emending means altering, so the letters of it's pearl are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone correcting a column of text with a pearl.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangular column projecting from a wall, a decorative pier.

clue.text: A small piece missing? That's unacceptable!

parts.note: a bit is a small piece
off means absent or missing, as in a day off

explanation.surface: Complaining that a little piece has gone, which is not on.
explanation.definitionFit: A British phrase for behaviour that is rather unfair or out of order.

clue.text: The chicken is utterly revolting

indicators.note: utterly is read as when uttered, meaning spoken out loud

parts.note: foul means disgusting, revolting

explanation.surface: A remark that the chicken tastes truly disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like an intensifier but means 'when uttered', the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic bird kept for eggs and meat, such as a hen.

clue.text: Lays claim to the luggage

definitions.meaning: in British usage to claim first
cases and holdalls taken on a trip

explanation.surface: Someone claims the suitcases.
explanation.definitionFit: British children shout 'bags' to claim something; suitcases are also so called.

clue.text: Make a bonfire and collapse

definitions.meaning: to let a fire consume itself completely

explanation.surface: Lighting a fire, then fainting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire left to finish consumes itself; exhaustion from stress is the noun.

clue.text: Foolishly agrees to use a lubricant

indicators.note: foolishly means done in a silly way, so the letters of agrees are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone unwisely consents to using oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily fat smeared on moving parts to reduce friction.

clue.text: A banker constantly going in two directions

indicators.note: going in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: S and N are compass directions, south and north
ever means always, constantly

explanation.surface: A bank worker always travelling both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is a river, something with banks; the Severn is Britain's longest river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, so crosswords call it a banker; this is the longest in Britain.

clue.text: Extra lean

explanation.surface: Additional thin meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve item is additional; a thin frame is slender too.

clue.text: All employees use coercive measures

parts.note: to work something is to use or operate it
force means compulsion or coercion

explanation.surface: Staff are made to comply by strong-arm tactics.
explanation.definitionFit: The total staff or labour of a company.

clue.text: Priest always less restricted

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A clergyman who is forever less constrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Having more liberty is the comparative of unconstrained.

clue.text: Cost borne by unpopular amateur

parts.note: out means out of favour or unfashionable
lay means non-professional, as in a layman

explanation.surface: An expense paid by a disliked non-professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Money spent on something is an expenditure.

clue.text: Media reporting makes bloke see red

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man, a bloke
to see red is to become furious, to rage

explanation.surface: Press reports make a man furious.
explanation.definitionFit: The extent to which news outlets report on something.

clue.text: Free to return to cathedral — but fearfully

indicators.note: to return means to go back, so the word for free is read backwards

parts.note: to rid is to free
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Released to go back to the cathedral, but with dread.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is an English cathedral city near Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadfully or terribly, as in a dire warning.

clue.text: Operator without time to get fish

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a surgeon operates on patients

explanation.surface: A surgeon goes without his tea break to catch a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a deletion but means 'outside' here.
explanation.definitionFit: A large fish whose roe is caviar.
